nodes.title: Algebraization: the generic fibre is quasi-projective and a union of Shimura varieties
nodes.statement: Let K be neat, Case A or C. The algebraic space M^ad_K ⊗_{F₀} ℂ is a quasi-projective scheme, and the analytic isomorphism ⊔_i u^{(i)} of M3/uniformization-morphism is the analytification of a unique isomorphism of ℂ-schemes ⊔_{i ∈ ker¹(ℚ,G)} Sh_K(G^{(i)}, X)_ℂ ≅ M^ad_K ⊗ ℂ, where Sh_K(G^{(i)}, X)_ℂ is the quasi-projective algebraization of ShimuraVarieties V2–V3. Each piece is open and closed; the identification is compatible with level change, Hecke operators and the universal families. This uses neither the integral compactification of ShimuraCompactifications C5 nor a blanket statement that M^ad_K is one Sh_K(G, X).
proofSteps: Choose an étale atlas U → M^ad_K ⊗ ℂ by a scheme with quasi-projective affine pieces; the composite U^an → ⊔ Sh_K^an is holomorphic between quasi-projective varieties of which the target is the Baily–Borel quasi-projective variety (ShimuraVarieties V2).

Borel's algebraicity theorem (ShimuraVarieties V3) makes each U^an → Sh_K^an algebraic; the maps agree on overlaps U ×_M U, so they descend to an algebraic morphism M^ad_K ⊗ ℂ → ⊔ Sh_K(G^{(i)}, X)_ℂ (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension: descent of local-isomorphism comparisons along étale presentations).

To recover an isomorphism from the algebraized map, compare its local rings using the faithful flat algebraic-to-analytic local-ring maps (ComplexComparisonPartII C0), deduce étaleness, and use the algebraic-space local-isomorphism criterion plus the bijection on geometric points. Proper GAGA at C3/C4 cannot be applied directly to these nonproper PEL spaces. Borel algebraicity remains the V3 supplier and the analytic carrier remains unresolved.

nodes.title: Type D: disconnected similitude groups and the moduli problem
nodes.statement: For a rational PEL datum with a type-D simple factor, G is disconnected. Kottwitz §8 gives the complex double-coset description using the full G and its real conjugacy class of h in the p-integral setting after verifying the component obstruction needed in Lemma 7.2. The precise comparison with Shimura varieties of G° is an open target: no unrestricted identification or finite-component-group quotient theorem is asserted in this packet.

p ≠ 2 where integral statements are made

Retain the full disconnected G in the double-coset problem. Establishing a quotient formula in terms of G° requires rational and adelic component images, stabilizers, and the subgroup K∩G°; it does not follow merely from the finite number of real components. This is part of the recorded open target.

Record the G° comparison and its indexing as an explicit gap. Kottwitz does not prove that comparison here; the official Lan thesis errata removes the vague change-of-primes failure claim in Remark 1.4.4.3. Milne warns against silently replacing G by G°.

nodes.title: The moduli Galois action on CM points is Shimura reciprocity
nodes.statement: Let K be neat, (T, h) a special pair of (G, X) (ShimuraData:D4/special-pair) with reflex field E(T, h) ⊃ F₀, and x = [h, g] ∈ Sh_K(G^{(i)}, X)(ℂ) ⊂ M^ad_K(ℂ) a special point (the abelian variety A_x has CM by a CM algebra containing the image of T). nodes.statement: In Case A with n odd, let z ∈ ker¹(ℚ, Z) ≅ ker¹(ℚ, G), represented by a totally positive a ∈ F₀^× which is a unit at the places above p, together with β = (β_ℓ) ∈ (𝔸_f^p ⊗ F)^× with a·N_{F/F₀}(β_ℓ) ∈ ℚ_ℓ^× for every ℓ ≠ p. λ ∘ i(a) is a polarization because a is totally positive and in the centre; the Rosati involution is unchanged since a* = a; the multiplier changes by a, compensated by β on level structures.
Equivariance and compatibility with sheaves are formal; the image of S^{(1)} is S^{(i)} because H₁ changes by the twist of the form by a (class z_i).

nodes.title: Finiteness, normality and flatness of the normalized models
nodes.statement: In the setting of M4/higher-level-normalization: 𝔐_{K_pK^p} is finite over 𝔐, normal, and flat over O_{F₀,v}; its special fibre need not be reduced, smooth or equidimensional beyond what flatness gives (it is equidimensional of the same dimension as the generic fibre).
proofSteps: Finiteness: 𝔐 is of finite type over O_{F₀,v}, hence excellent and Nagata (SchemeAndStackFoundations key/excellent-schemes); the normalization of a Nagata scheme in a reduced finite-type scheme is finite (Stacks Tag 03GR), applied on an étale atlas (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension: finiteness of normalisation under excellence).
Normality: by construction (the integral closure of a normal ring in a reduced algebra whose total ring of fractions is a product of fields is normal).

Flatness over O_{F₀,v}: 𝔐_{K_pK^p} is reduced with every irreducible component dominating Spec O_{F₀,v} (the structure sheaf is contained in the pushforward from the generic fibre), so its local rings are torsion-free over the DVR O_{F₀,v}, hence flat (Stacks Tag 0539).

nodes.title: The CM moduli scheme T_p(W₀, K^p₀)
nodes.statement: Let F be a CM field, p unramified in F, Φ a CM type, W₀ a rational skew-hermitian space over O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p) of rank 1 and type Φ (M0/skew-hermitian-space), and K^p₀ ⊂ T₀(𝔸^{∞,p}) open compact. T¹_p(W₀, K^p₀) is the presheaf on locally noetherian O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)-schemes sending S to equivalence classes of (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p): (A₀, λ₀) a unitary O_F-abelian scheme of signature type Φ with λ₀ p-principal and η₀^p a K^p₀-level structure (a π₁-invariant K^p₀-orbit of similitudes W₀ ⊗ 𝔸^{∞,p} ≅ H₁^ét(A₀s, 𝔸^{∞,p})), modulo prime-to-p O_F-linear quasi-isogenies carrying (λ₀, η₀^p) to (cλ₀', η₀^{p'}) for some c ∈ ℤ_(p)^×. For K^p₀ neat it is represented by a scheme finite étale over O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p). The map w : T¹_p(ℂ) → ker¹(T₀) sends a point to the similarity class of H₁(A₀(ℂ), ℤ_(p)); T_p(W₀, K^p₀) is the minimal open and closed subscheme containing w⁻¹(class of W₀). T₀(𝔸^{∞,p}) acts by a·(A₀, λ₀, η₀^p) = (A₀, λ₀, η₀^p ∘ a) with stabilizer T₀(ℤ_(p))K^p₀.
proofSteps: T¹_p is the rational moduli problem M^rat_{K^p₀} (M1/rational-moduli-problem with □ = {p}) for the rank-one unitary PEL datum of signature Φ, with reflex field F_Φ (M0/generalized-cm-type).

Representability by a finite étale scheme: M2/representability (smooth of relative dimension Σ p_τ q_τ = 0, so étale) and M2/properness-when-division (End_F(W₀) = F is a field, so proper); a proper étale algebraic space with quasi-finite fibres is a finite étale scheme. LTXZZ states this as known without proof; this supplies it.
The map w and T_p: M0/rank-one-skew-hermitian-classification identifies similarity classes with ker¹(T₀); the fibre w⁻¹(W₀) is a union of components.
The T₀(𝔸^{∞,p})-action by changing η₀^p, with stabilizer computed from M2/no-automorphisms-at-neat-level.
acceptance: F imaginary quadratic: T_p(W₀, K^p₀) is a finite étale O_F ⊗ ℤ_(p)-scheme whose ℂ-points are CM elliptic curves with level structure.

nodes.title: Galois structure of T_p(W₀, K^p₀)
nodes.statement: In the setting of M4/cm-moduli-scheme with K^p₀ neat, the morphism T_p(W₀, K^p₀) → Spec(O_{F_Φ} ⊗ ℤ_(p)) is a Galois (finite étale torsor) cover with Galois group T₀(𝔸^{∞,p})/T₀(ℤ_(p))K^p₀ acting as in M4/cm-moduli-scheme; this group is finite.
proofSteps: Finiteness of T₀(𝔸^{∞,p})/T₀(ℤ_(p))K^p₀: it injects into T₀(ℚ)\T₀(𝔸^∞)/T₀(ℤ_p)K^p₀, finite (class-group finiteness for tori).
On ℂ-points, T_p(ℂ) is a torsor under this group (M3/complex-points for the torus datum: one G(ℚ)-orbit after fixing the similarity class).
The Galois action on ℂ-points commutes with T₀(𝔸^{∞,p}) and is given by reciprocity (M4/cm-points-reciprocity), so the cover is Galois with the stated group acting by deck transformations.

nodes.title: 𝔗-invariant cohomology and the 𝔗-trace map
nodes.statement: Let 𝔗 be the groupoid of the finite group Γ := T₀(𝔸^{∞,p})/T₀(ℤ_(p))K^p₀ and X : 𝔗 → Sch a functor (a scheme X(∗) with Γ-action), L a coefficient ring. H^i_𝔗(X, L(j)) ⊂ H^i_ét(X(∗), L(j)) and H^i_{𝔗,c}(X, L(j)) ⊂ H^i_{ét,c}(X(∗), L(j)) are the maximal submodules on which Γ acts trivially (invariants, not coinvariants). If κ is algebraically closed of characteristic p, L is p-coprime, X(∗) is smooth of finite type of dimension d over κ and Γ acts freely on π₀(X(∗)), the 𝔗-trace ∫^𝔗_X : H^{2d}_{𝔗,c}(X(∗), L(d)) → L is the composite of the inclusion into H^{2d}_c(X(∗), L(d)), the projection to ⊕_Y H^{2d}_c(Y, L(d)) over a set {Y} of representatives of Γ-orbits on components, and Σ tr_Y; it is independent of the representatives.
hypotheses: Γ finite acting freely on components for the trace
proofSteps: Define invariant submodules functorially in X (functor on ℭ × 𝔗 composed with the projection).

Trace: on a Γ-invariant class, the traces on Y and on gY agree (tr is compatible with the isomorphism g : Y → gY), so the sum over representatives does not depend on choices; no division by |Γ| occurs.
Étale cohomology with compact support and the trace map tr_Y for smooth connected Y of dimension d are imported (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2).
acceptance: For Γ trivial and connected X, the orbit trace equals the usual trace. A nontrivial group acting trivially on connected components does not satisfy the freeness hypothesis.

nodes.title: Siegel PEL data of every genus and polarization type
nodes.statement: For g ≥ 1 and positive integers d₁ | d₂ | … | d_g (the type D), the Siegel PEL datum of genus g and type D is (ℤ, id, L_D, ⟨·,·⟩_D, h): L_D = ℤ^{2g} with basis e₁, …, e_g, f₁, …, f_g and ⟨e_i, f_j⟩_D = d_i δ_{ij}·2π√−1, ⟨e_i, e_j⟩ = ⟨f_i, f_j⟩ = 0 (values in ℤ(1)), and h(√−1) = J_D with J_D e_i = f_i, J_D f_i = −e_i, so that (1/2π√−1)⟨x, J_D y⟩ = Σ_i d_i (x_{e_i} y_{e_i} + x_{f_i} y_{f_i}) is positive definite (for D = (1, …, 1) and Mathlib's Matrix.J, whose form has ψ(e_i, f_i) = −1, the same structure is h(√−1) = −J). Its similitude group is G = GSp(L_D) (≅ GSp_{2g} over ℚ), Case C, I_bad = 1, Disc = 1, [L_D^# : L_D] = (d₁⋯d_g)², reflex field ℚ, signatures (g, g), and the bad primes for level n are those dividing n·d_g. Its Shimura datum is ShimuraData:D5/siegel-datum.
proofSteps: Write down L_D, ⟨·,·⟩_D and h; check Condition 1.2.1.2 by computing the real form (block-diagonal positive definite).
Compute L_D^# = ⊕ (d_i⁻¹ℤ e_i ⊕ d_i⁻¹ℤ f_i) and the index; type is recovered by the Smith normal form of the Gram matrix (Tau Ceti Matrix.exists_smith_normal_form_of_det_ne_zero).
Identify G₁ with Sp(L_D) (for D = 1, Tau Ceti Symplectic.groupScheme) and the Shimura datum with D5's Siegel datum; reflex field ℚ because V₀ is determined by its dimension g (M0/reflex-field).

nodes.title: Siegel moduli A_{g,D,n} for every genus
nodes.statement: For the Siegel datum of genus g and type D and n ≥ 1, A_{g,D,n} := M_{U(n)} over ℤ[1/(n d_g)] is the moduli problem of abelian schemes A/S of relative dimension g with a polarization λ whose kernel is étale-locally ≅ (⊕_i ℤ/d_i)², and a symplectic level-n structure (α_n, ν_n) of type L_D. nodes.title: Genus one: PEL Siegel moduli versus the modular curves of #81
nodes.statement: For g = 1, D = (1) and n ≥ 3, there is an isomorphism over ℤ[1/n] between A_{1,1,n} = M_{U(n)} and the fine moduli scheme Y(n) of elliptic curves with full level-n structure of the Tau Ceti ModularCurves roadmap (#81), sending (A, λ, α_n, ν_n) to (A with its unique principal polarization, (P, Q) = (α_n(e₁), α_n(f₁))) with the Weil-pairing convention e_n(P, Q) = ν_n(⟨e₁, f₁⟩ mod n), where ⟨e₁, f₁⟩ = 2π√−1 generates ℤ(1); over ℤ[1/n, ζ_n], the fibre ν_n(1) = ζ is Y(n, ζ) of ModularCurves layer 5B (full ordered bases with fixed pairing). One-dimensional abelian schemes are elliptic curves (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1, via the Weierstrass presentation of #81), and the comparison respects universal objects and the Hecke action of GL₂(ℤ/n) (row-versus-column conventions pinned as in ShimuraVarieties V8).
proofSteps: Elliptic curves over S = abelian schemes of relative dimension 1 (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A1); every such has a unique principal polarization (the canonical one), so λ is determined and D = (1) forces it.
A symplectic level-n structure for the standard pairing is an ordered basis (P, Q) of E[n] with e_n(P, Q) = ν_n(ζ_n^{univ}); liftability is automatic for principal polarizations (L self-dual).

Match with the Katz–Mazur [Γ(n)] moduli problem and Y(n, ζ) (ModularCurves layers 3C, 4A, 5B) and the Cartier–Nishi Weil pairing (layer 2E); the sign convention e_n(P, Q) versus e_n(Q, P) is fixed by ⟨e₁, f₁⟩ = +1.
Universal objects correspond by the universal properties; the GL₂(ℤ/n)-actions agree after the transpose convention of ShimuraVarieties V8.

nodes.title: Unitary PEL data over CM fields with prescribed signatures
nodes.statement: Let K be a CM field with maximal totally real subfield K⁺, Φ a CM type, (V, H) a hermitian space over K of dimension n with signature (r_τ, s_τ) at each τ ∈ Φ (r_τ + s_τ = n), and δ ∈ K^× with δ̄ = −δ and Im τ(δ) > 0 for τ ∈ Φ. The unitary PEL datum is (O_K, c, L, ⟨·,·⟩, h): ⟨x, y⟩ := Tr_{K/ℚ}(δ H(x, y))·2π√−1 on an O_K-lattice L ⊂ V with ⟨L, L⟩ ⊂ ℤ(1), and h(√−1) acting on V ⊗_{K,τ} ℂ ≅ ℂ^n by diag(√−1·1_{r_τ}, −√−1·1_{s_τ}) in an H-orthogonal basis (with the sign fixed by the positivity of (1/√−1)⟨x, h(√−1)y⟩). Its similitude group is GU(V) (Case A), I_bad = 1, its signatures are (p_τ, q_τ) = (r_τ, s_τ) with Ψ = Σ_{τ∈Φ} (r_τ τ + s_τ τ̄), its reflex field is F_Ψ, its relative dimension is Σ_{τ∈Φ} r_τ s_τ, and its good primes at level n are those not dividing n·disc(K)·[L^# : L].
hypotheses: K CM, (V, H) hermitian of dimension n
δ totally imaginary with Im τ(δ) > 0 on Φ
proofSteps: Check alternation and adjointness: ⟨x, x⟩ = Tr(δ H(x, x)) = 0 since δ H(x, x) is totally imaginary; ⟨ax, y⟩ = ⟨x, āy⟩ (M0/hermitian-space dictionary).
Check Condition 1.2.1.2: on V ⊗_{K,τ} ℂ the real form is 2 Im τ(δ)·(±Re H) with signs matching the signature, positive definite by the choice of h (Kottwitz Lemma 4.3 signature argument).
Compute signatures, reflex field (M0/generalized-cm-type: F_Ψ), relative dimension (M2/kodaira-spencer-dimension) and bad primes (Disc(O_K) = disc(K) by M0/order-discriminant).
acceptance: K imaginary quadratic, n = 3, signature (2, 1): Picard datum, reflex field K, dimension 2.
K imaginary quadratic, signature (1, 1): reflex field ℚ, dimension 1.

Similarly the unitary datum with L = O_K ⊕ O_K ⊕ 𝔭O_K (non-self-dual at a prime 𝔭 | p) has p bad.

nodes.title: Level-forgetting and Hecke maps are finite étale
nodes.statement: For open compact H' ⊂ H ⊂ G(Ẑ^□), the forgetful morphism M_{H'} → M_H (M1/hecke-action) is representable, finite and étale. If H is neat and H' ⊲ H, it is a Galois cover of algebraic spaces with group H/H' acting freely by Hecke translation. For g ∈ G(𝔸^{∞,□}), the two maps of the Hecke correspondence M_H ← M_{H ∩ gHg⁻¹} → M_H are finite étale.
proofSteps: Étale-locally on S, an integral level-H structure lifts to an H'-structure, and the set of lifts is a torsor under H_n/H'_n for n with U^□(n) ⊂ H' (Lan Definition 1.3.7.8): the fibre is a finite étale scheme.
Representability by schemes: the fibre over an object is the finite étale scheme of H'-orbits refining α_H.
Neat case: H/H' acts on M_{H'} over M_H, freely because objects have no automorphisms (M2/no-automorphisms-at-neat-level), with quotient M_H.
acceptance: Siegel g = 1: Y(nm) → Y(n) is finite étale Galois with group the kernel of GL₂(ℤ/nm) → GL₂(ℤ/n) (modulo ±1 at non-neat level).

nodes.title: The PEL moduli stack at arbitrary level and its presentations
nodes.statement: Let H ⊂ G(Ẑ^□) be any open compact subgroup (not necessarily neat) and H' ⊲ H a neat open normal subgroup. Then the action of the finite group H/H' on the algebraic space M_{H'} (by Hecke translation) gives an isomorphism of stacks [M_{H'}/(H/H')] ≅ M_H. Consequently M_H is a separated Deligne–Mumford stack, smooth of finite type over S₀, with finite inertia; the presentation is independent of H' up to canonical equivalence. The universal object of M_{H'} descends to the universal object of the stack M_H.
proofSteps: Quotient stack [M_{H'}/(H/H')] of an algebraic space by a finite group is a DM stack (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.4: quotient stacks; RS-27 leaves the PEL instance to this layer).
Construct M_{H'} → M_H as an H/H'-torsor of fibred categories (M6/level-forgetting-maps: the fibre is the set of H'-refinements of α_H, an H/H'-torsor), hence [M_{H'}/(H/H')] ≅ M_H.
Inertia: Aut of an object is a subgroup of the stabilizer in H/H' (finite); separatedness from M2/isom-scheme.
Independence of H': for H'' ⊂ H' both neat normal, the presentations are compatible via M_{H''} → M_{H'}.
acceptance: Siegel g = 1, H = GL₂(ℤ̂^□) (no level): M_H = [Y(n)/GL₂(ℤ/n)] over ℤ[1/n] for n ≥ 3, the moduli stack of elliptic curves.

nodes.title: The stack 𝔄_g of principally polarized abelian schemes over ℤ
nodes.statement: Let 𝔄_g be the fibred category over Sch/ℤ of principally polarized abelian schemes (A, λ) of relative dimension g. Then 𝔄_g is a smooth separated Deligne–Mumford stack of finite type over Spec ℤ of relative dimension g(g+1)/2, with universal abelian scheme A^univ → 𝔄_g. Over ℤ[1/n] (n ≥ 3), 𝔄_g ⊗ ℤ[1/n] ≅ [A_{g,1,n}/GSp_{2g}(ℤ/n)] (M5/siegel-moduli with the Hecke action of G(ℤ/n) = G(Ẑ^□)/U^□(n)), and 𝔄_g is glued from the presentations over ℤ[1/3] and ℤ[1/4].
proofSteps: For a principal polarization, the liftability condition at level H = G(Ẑ^□) is automatic (L self-dual), so 𝔄_g ⊗ ℤ[1/n] is M_{G(Ẑ^□)} for the Siegel datum with □ = {p ∤ n}; apply M6/arbitrary-level-stack with H' = U^□(n), n ≥ 3.
The open substacks over ℤ[1/3] and ℤ[1/4] cover 𝔄_g and agree on the overlap ℤ[1/12] (both are 𝔄_g ⊗ ℤ[1/12]); the stack property is local on the base (M1/effective-descent).
Smoothness and relative dimension from M2/representability and M2/kodaira-spencer-dimension; universal family from M2/universal-family descended (M6/arbitrary-level-stack).
acceptance: g = 1: 𝔄_1 is the moduli stack of elliptic curves over ℤ.

nodes.title: Finite type of the stack of polarized abelian schemes of degree d² over ℤ
nodes.statement: For g, d ≥ 1 let 𝔄_{g,d} be the fibred category over Sch/ℤ of abelian schemes of relative dimension g with a polarization of degree d² (no restriction relating d to the residue characteristics). Then 𝔄_{g,d} is an algebraic stack of finite type over Spec ℤ with finite unramified diagonal (a separated Deligne–Mumford stack); over ℤ[1/n], n ≥ 3, its rigidification by full symplectic level-n structure of each type D with d₁⋯d_g = d is an algebraic space of finite type. For p | d the stack is not claimed to be smooth over ℤ_(p).
proofSteps: Stack and diagonal: M1/effective-descent and M2/isom-scheme apply verbatim (they do not use goodness of primes).

A polarization morphism and an ample line bundle inducing it are different moduli data. Étale-locally choose an ample symmetric L with χ(L)=d and use L^⊗3 to obtain a bounded Hilbert presentation. The PGL quotient initially classifies (A,L), not (A,λ). To reach 𝔄_{g,d}, forget the relative Pic^0 torsor of choices of L and verify descent, finite type and the diagonal after that passage. Import the Picard and quotient interfaces from A2/R09.2/R09.4; their precise scope, including p|d, is an open gap. A GIT citation alone does not prove this passage.
Rigidified level: as in M6/level-forgetting-maps.

For p | d, 𝔄_{g,d} ⊗ 𝔽_p is of finite type but in general not smooth.

nodes.title: Coarse moduli spaces of PEL stacks
nodes.statement: For any open compact H, the stack M_H (finite inertia, M6/arbitrary-level-stack) has a coarse moduli space π : M_H → M_H^c: a separated algebraic space of finite type over S₀, universal for morphisms to algebraic spaces, with π bijective on geometric points; π is an isomorphism when H is neat; the formation of M_H^c commutes with flat base change S₀' → S₀ (and with arbitrary base change in the tame case where |H/H'| is invertible). Locally, M_H^c ≅ M_{H'}/(H/H') for a neat normal H'. The same holds for 𝔄_g and 𝔄_{g,d} over ℤ: the coarse space A_g of 𝔄_g satisfies A_g(K̄) = {principally polarized abelian varieties over K̄}/≅ for every algebraically closed field K̄, and a principally polarized A over a field K has a moduli point x_A ∈ A_g(K).
proofSteps: Apply the finite-inertia coarse-space theorem of AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.5 (RS-27 owner record: PEL coarse spaces are owned here, by R09.5's theorem).
For the quotient presentation, M_H^c = M_{H'}/(H/H') (quotient of an algebraic space by a finite group).
Base change statements as available in R09.5 (flat; tame); points over algebraically closed fields by bijectivity.
acceptance: g = 1: the coarse space of 𝔄_1 is the j-line 𝔸¹_ℤ (ModularCurves layer 9E).
Neat H: M_H^c = M_H.

nodes.title: Field of moduli of a polarized abelian variety with PEL structure
nodes.statement: Let k be a field with separable closure k^s and ξ = (A, λ, i, α) an object of M_H (or of 𝔄_g, 𝔄_{g,d}) over k^s. Its field of moduli k(ξ) is the fixed field of the subgroup {σ ∈ Gal(k^s/k) : σ^*ξ ≅ ξ}. Equivalently, k(ξ) is the residue field of the image point of ξ in the coarse space M_H^c (at a point with residue field separable over k). If ξ has a model over a subextension k₁, then k(ξ) ⊂ k₁; a k(ξ)-rational coarse point does not by itself give a model over k(ξ) (M6/forms-and-descent-obstruction).
proofSteps: Define the stabilizer of the isomorphism class; it is open (ξ is defined over a finite extension).
Identify with the residue field of the coarse point: σ fixes the coarse point iff σ^*ξ ≅ ξ (bijectivity of M_H → M_H^c on geometric points).
Models give inclusions: if ξ ≅ (ξ₁)_{k^s} with ξ₁ over k₁, then Gal(k^s/k₁) fixes the class.
acceptance: Elliptic curves over ℚ̄: the field of moduli is ℚ(j).

nodes.title: Rational coarse points versus rational families: forms and the descent obstruction
nodes.statement: (a) Let ξ be an object of M_H (or 𝔄_g) over a field K and K'/K finite Galois. The K-forms of ξ split by K' (objects ξ' over K with ξ'_{K'} ≅ ξ_{K'}, up to K-isomorphism) are in bijection with the pointed set H¹(Gal(K'/K), Aut_{K'}(ξ_{K'})). (b) For a point x ∈ M_H^c(k), the objects over k mapping to x form the sections of the residual gerbe 𝒢_x → Spec k, a gerbe with band whose geometric fiber is the finite étale automorphism group Aut_{k^s}(ξ_x); in the nonneutral case this band need not be represented by a canonically chosen k-group; x lifts to an object over k iff 𝒢_x is neutral. If objects have no automorphisms (neat H), every k-point of M_H^c = M_H lifts uniquely. (c) Hence, for a level-free stack such as 𝔄_g, a K-rational coarse point is not by itself a polarized abelian variety over K; consumers (R28.1, R35.5) must use objects, or a rigidifying level with its field extension.
proofSteps: (a) Galois descent for quasi-projective schemes with ample descent data (M1/effective-descent): a descent datum on ξ_{K'} is a 1-cocycle in Aut_{K'}(ξ); twisting identifies forms with H¹ (standard nonabelian cohomology of a finite group).
(b) The residual gerbe of a point of a DM stack with finite inertia (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.4 gerbes and residual gerbes; R09.5 coarse spaces); neutral iff it has a section.
Neat case: trivial band, so the gerbe is trivial.
acceptance: For 𝔄_1 over a field of characteristic ≠ 2, 3 every point lifts (WeierstrassCurve.ofJ), and its forms are the quadratic (and, for j = 0, 1728, quartic/sextic) twists, classified by H¹(Gal, Aut(E)).

nodes.title: Models over a bounded extension of the field of moduli (level three)
nodes.statement: Let (A, λ) be a polarized abelian variety of dimension g over ℚ̄ with field of moduli F = ℚ(A, λ) (M6/field-of-moduli). Let F' be the compositum of ℚ(e^{2πi/3}) and the field of moduli of (A, λ) together with a basis of A[3]. Then (A, λ) has a model over F' (rigidity of level 3), all endomorphisms and polarizations of A are defined over F', and [F' : F] ≤ 2·3^{4g²}. The rigidity used is that of the polarized pair with full level 3 (M2/rigidity), not of A alone.
proofSteps: The pair (A, λ) with a full level-3 structure has no automorphisms (M2/rigidity), so its field of moduli is a field of definition (M6/forms-and-descent-obstruction (b) with trivial band).
Degree bound: the field of moduli with a basis of A[3] has degree at most |GL_{2g}(𝔽₃)| ≤ 3^{4g²} over F, and adjoining ζ₃ contributes a factor 2.

B[3] ≅ Hom(A[3], μ₃) for the dual B is then F'-rational; endomorphisms and polarizations are defined over a field over which A[3] and B[3] are rational (Silverberg's theorem for n ≥ 3, cited by Tsimerman as [19, Prop. 2.3]; requested from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A6).

nodes.title: The Hodge bundle and the Hodge line of the universal family
nodes.statement: For an abelian scheme f : A → S with zero section e, ω_{A/S} := e^*Ω¹_{A/S} = f_*Ω¹_{A/S} is locally free of rank g (dual to Lie_{A/S}) and the Hodge line is ω̄_{A/S} := det ω_{A/S} = ∧^g ω_{A/S}. On the stack M_H (or 𝔄_g, 𝔄_{g,d}) the Hodge bundle ω and Hodge line ω̄ of the universal object are vector bundles on the stack, pulled back along classifying maps; on the fine space M_H (H neat) they are bundles on an algebraic space; ω is the Hodge filtration piece of H^1_dR of the universal family (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4). gaps.title: Nonabelian Galois cohomology, ker¹ and the Hasse principle
gaps.detail: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 (merged 2026-10-06) plans G-torsors over a field, Kneser's vanishing H¹(F_v, G) = 1 and the Hasse principle for semisimple simply connected G (its own gap records their proofs); M3/hasse-principle-cases imports those nodes. No atlas layer owns the rest of the Galois cohomology of linear algebraic groups that this roadmap uses: the twisting classification of forms of a skew-Hermitian B-module by H¹(ℚ, G) for connected reductive (not simply connected) G, ker¹(ℚ, G) as a pointed set and its finiteness (Borel–Serre, cited by Kottwitz as [BS]), Kottwitz's ker¹(ℚ, G) = ker¹(ℚ, G/G^der) for G with simply connected derived group, and Tate–Nakayama duality for ker¹ and ker² of tori. Mathlib's CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups.H1 is a Čech-type nonabelian H¹ (a near miss) and Tau Ceti's ContCohomology.H1 has abelian coefficients only. EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.0/ET.5 and LTXZZ Remark 3.5.2 need the same inputs. A restructure entry proposes an owner.

A source such as Lan's 'Example-based introduction to Shimura varieties' §5.1.3 (not obtained: the author's site refused access) is needed.

gaps.title: Suggested signatures and semantic fidelity (REV-PELModuli)
gaps.detail: All targets were independently audited. The current file has numerous weakened or unrelated interfaces: Albert types are an unused label on Wedderburn decomposition, goodPrime.unramified_reflex only proves nondivisibility of an input integer, hodge/toShimuraDatum do not use pinned carriers, QuasiIsogeny need not be invertible and IsPrimeTo only checks denominators, O-actions need not be ring homomorphisms, levels are not tied to actual torsion, neatness omits torsion generated by ratios of eigenvalues, comparison/CM/Galois APIs take unrelated arguments, and universal-family classification lacks the classifying pullback. Missing source hypotheses and exact named interfaces are enumerated in REV-PELModuli. Clear finite-dimensionality, J-adjointness, full-basis, CM-type-rank and finite Galois hypotheses and named tests were repaired, but these do not establish remaining semantics. No declaration is certified as formalised; implementationStatus stays unchecked. Repair at target level, importing the actual pinned carriers and leaving unavailable conditions explicitly out rather than admitting false substitute statements.

sourceIssues.locator: §8, 'PEL data' and 'PEL Shimura varieties', pp. 87–88 (2017 revision)
sourceIssues.printed: As h is nontrivial, SV3 follows from the fact that G^ad is simple. [...] The pair (G, X) satisfies the conditions SV1–4.
sourceIssues.correction: SV3 holds only when the projection of h to every ℚ-simple factor of G^ad is nontrivial. For a simple PEL datum of type (A) whose hermitian form is definite at every real place (signature (n, 0) everywhere with n ≥ 2), h(ℂ^×) is central, its projection to the ℚ-simple group G^ad = PU is trivial and G^ad(ℝ) is compact, so SV3 fails and (G, X) is not a Shimura datum (X is a point). Rank n=1 is a torus: its adjoint group is trivial and SV3 is vacuous. This finding concerns the September 2017 author revision, not a verified assertion about the 2005 publication.
sourceIssues.reason: For signature (n, 0) at every τ, h(z) acts on V ⊗_{K,τ} ℂ by z and on the conjugate part by z̄, i.e. through the centre K ⊗ ℝ = ∏ ℂ of End_B(V ⊗ ℝ); so ad ∘ h is trivial, while Milne's axiom SV3 (§5) reads 'G^ad has no ℚ-factor on which the projection of h is trivial'. 'h nontrivial' as a map to G does not imply nontrivial in G^ad.

review.notes: Independent target-level review: all 91 node source locators/excerpts and hypotheses, all 67 pinned baseline statements, closure and direct suppliers, APIs, named tests, planets, library audit, RS ownership decisions and RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/3 were checked. Clear source and signature corrections are recorded in REV-PELModuli.md. All stages are partial. Every whole-node verdict remains unverifiable because the proposed carriers/signatures omit or weaken target mathematics; an admitted elaborating statement alone is not verification. Five sourceIssues are confirmed with their version scope. This is a completed negative review, not an unfinished review checkpoint.

checked.note: Source definition checked. reducedTrace is admitted on arbitrary rings without the finite semisimple carrier; center_stable omits the packet’s simple-factor and totally-real/CM conclusions. Import existing star and trace ingredients; the full API is not represented.

The source classifies positive involutions, not merely algebras. The Lean type labels are unconstrained and its conclusion is only Wedderburn–Artin, already in Mathlib; no type/involution classification is stated.

Source requires a full integral order and an integral basis. Lean disc_eq_index_diffInv takes an arbitrary rational independent family, for which integrality fails (basis 1/2 in Q gives discriminant 1/4); the maximality API lacks full-order hypotheses.

Finite generation was added to the carrier. The polarization-type interface still does not tie elementary divisors to a block basis or the Smith form; import the pinned dual-lattice and Smith-form results with their actual hypotheses.

The source allows zero L and a nonfaithful O-action. The carrier must keep those cases while rationalization separately imposes faithful scalar extension; its tests and compatibility with the existing Tau Ceti symplectic/Hodge carriers remain incomplete.

Added finite-dimensional semisimple B, positivity and real adjoint compatibility; restricted faithful rationalization. The arbitrary spanning O-to-B map is still not an identification B = O tensor Q, and the full p-integral datum is not faithfully expressed.

Corrected uniqueness to flat R and nonzero L; added a proved F5 counterexample and errata citation. The general group-scheme/base-change interface and actual compatibility with the pinned constant-form group still need repair.

Source describes algebraic groups and their derived groups/components. Admitted group and component data do not supply these scheme-theoretic statements, and labels are not tied to the Albert decomposition.

Source bad-prime conditions checked. goodPrime_unramified_reflex does not express the local field extension being unramified; arithmetic nondivisibility of an input discriminant is insufficient without tying it to the reflex field.

The stated polarized Hodge structure is replaced by an isotropy assertion. Tau Ceti already has almost-complex-to-Hodge and Weil-operator polarization results; their finite/integral carriers and full invariance hypotheses must be imported.
Source SV3 restriction and rank-one exception checked. The Lean toShimuraDatum returns a Set, rather than the supplied Shimura datum with its axioms and the precise noncentrality condition.

The source embeddings belong to the centre of B and the Hodge representation. Lean allows an unrelated field and does not encode their eigenspace ranks or conjugate compatibility, so the signature and its rank API are not the packet construction.

Pinned generic polyCharpoly is the right ingredient. Suggested detPoly_exact states the split direct-sum case only, not equivariant short exact sequences; the affine free-module API does not supply the packet’s locally free sheaf and scheme base-change interfaces.

Added finite-dimensional C and spanning alpha to remove the zero-family counterexample. The suggested result still states only determinant classification, not all source conclusions and base-change hypotheses of this node.

The source reflex field is the coefficient field of the Hodge determinant of the datum. The trace is an admitted function without a represented restriction to V0, and unramified_reflex allows any subfield F acting on B rather than its centre (F = Q would force unramifiedness at every p).

The source compares the determinant coefficient field with the cocharacter stabilizer field. The suggested comparison does not identify the same datum and its cocharacter, so the fixed-field result does not realize the target.

Source polynomial-law equality checked. The suggested condition on a free module is only linear algebra until actual Lie(A), the order action, coefficient base map and their base changes are supplied.

Replaced the retracted F0-lattice descent with an auxiliary finite extension and finite-etale splitting, including nilpotent bases. Suggested spanning hypotheses were repaired, but that auxiliary integral model and its descent are still absent.

Corrected the uniqueness clause to exclude type D and kept the extra component condition for its second clause. The suggested symplectic Z-matrix result does not classify O-linear self-dual lattices with the prescribed multirank.

BPS Hypothesis 1.1.1 and its signatures above primes were read. The suggested field/signature data are not identified with the centre, involution or integral PEL data, and do not express the prime-indexed source equality.

Restricted the trace-to-PEL dictionary to rational F/Q data. The suggested arbitrary star algebra and module do not encode the source CM extension, finite locally free module, perfect pairing or the sharp construction over its actual base.

Recorded the LTXZZ zero-space convention (GU(0) as maps is trivial, unlike Lan’s pair group) and rational-only PEL conversion. The suggested arbitrary base algebra lacks the CM involution and nondegeneracy/similitude identifications required by the source.

The rank-one norm-torus classification needs genuine Galois H1 and its local-global kernel. The current cocycle data and requests do not supply that twisting classification; abelian continuous H1 is a near miss.
